status: Selected proposed research targets, not a certification of worldwide open-problem status
full_lists: Eight questions in article 1; nine in article 2; nine in article 3

questions.question: Can block noncollapse of the form g_(n+1)>=n^(-A)g_n be handled with a finite-parameter uniform theorem?
questions.reason: This would reach unbalanced recurrence classes beyond the current fixed annular ratio.
questions.first_step: Quantify the dependence of first-crossing sample addresses on a polynomially shrinking inner annulus.

questions.question: Can one bound the number of arcs and maximum witnessing index at a useful scale, and export checkable real-algebraic certificates?
questions.reason: The current effective theorem is a terminating existence search with enormous potential cost.
questions.first_step: Implement small recurrence boxes and a verified finite-membership checker.

questions.question: What replaces the subexponential degree condition when log Delta_N is proportional to N?
questions.reason: Local routing defeats subexponential losses; global window growth obstructs the same direct argument at positive exponential rate.
questions.first_step: Identify algebraic structure that reduces the number of realized local address vectors.

questions.question: Which infinite mixtures of exponential sequences or analytic observations admit one common positive-measure avoiding set?
questions.reason: Finite-dimensional parameter counting is essential in the current proof.
questions.first_step: Seek a finite approximation with an error smaller than a robust finite hitting margin.

questions.question: Can the Bell transfer be made uniform as n/m tends to zero, including depths of order n log n?
questions.reason: The new endpoint amplitude expansion does not itself justify a coefficient theorem in this regime.
questions.first_step: Obtain a contour or positive-measure transfer estimate uniform down to a quantified shrinking ratio.

questions.question: Can every Bell depth correction be summed with certified remainders, exposing all logarithmic cancellations in strict-chain asymptotics?
questions.reason: The present aggregation theorem identifies the leading amplitude only.
questions.first_step: Develop a discrete saddle expansion with derivatives of the amplitude uniformly controlled.

questions.question: Where is C(q) zero-free, and on which complex domains do the marked-chain asymptotics hold uniformly?
questions.reason: Holomorphic continuation on Re q>0 does not prevent zeros or control cancellation of coefficients.
questions.first_step: Separate amplitude zeros from competing saddle contributions.

questions.question: Can h and its derivatives be computed with rigorous enclosures and effective inversion errors?
questions.reason: The included independent decimal computations are diagnostic rather than interval-certified.
questions.first_step: Combine explicit Fatou-orbit truncation bounds with a validated Laplace-inversion contour.

questions.question: What is the maximal continuation domain of the tree residue and the nature of its first singularities?
questions.reason: The contraction gives only a local complex disk.
questions.first_step: Analyze the normalized odd iteration and its nearest singularities.

questions.question: Which higher even-cumulant boundaries are sharp, and which resonance or cancellation patterns are exceptional?
questions.reason: The Gaussian boundary is completely classified; higher renormalization currently has a sufficient criterion.
questions.first_step: Compute the first obstructing forcing and prove a noncancellation statement at the next boundary.

questions.question: Can the analytic residue method be extended to periodic, multitype, or random trees and finite-state channels?
questions.reason: The exact scalar parity cancellation may become an operator or symmetry condition.
questions.first_step: Treat periodic branching or a one-dimensional real character of a finite group channel.

questions.question: How do majority, the optimal estimator based on the sum, and the full posterior compare in the critical depth window?
questions.reason: The present theorem evaluates one specified decoder.
questions.first_step: Study the nonlinear posterior recursion on the same theta_n scale and derive compatible error bounds.
